claims.text: High-throughput computational screening can identify promising Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti alloy compositions based on phase-stability and L21 phase-fraction criteria.
High-throughput computational screening can optimize processing conditions for these alloys.
The initial Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti alloy has a BCC matrix.
The initial alloy is predisposed to ordering into the L21 phase.
Screening can identify compositions that form nanoscale L21 precipitates rather than extended antiphase domains.
The relevant composition window is Al below 25 at.% and Mn above 15 at.%.
Suitable synthesis includes arc-melting with repeated remelting, homogenization at approximately 1200 °C, and annealing at approximately 700 °C.
The morphology of the L21 ordering phase acts as a load-bearing component of the microstructure.
Deviation from perfect L21 stoichiometry promotes nanoscale L21 precipitation in the BCC matrix.
Nanoscale L21 precipitates enhance load transfer and precipitation strengthening relative to continuous antiphase domains.
Screened Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti alloys can retain high yield strength at elevated temperature.
Alloys designed by this method will exhibit refined microstructures containing nanoscale L21 precipitates.
The screened alloys have high-temperature yield strength superior to traditional alloy systems.
The high-temperature yield-strength enhancement is on the order of hundreds of MPa.
Traditional baseline alloys form BCC plus continuous L21, D03, or B2 ordered phases and lack the intentionally refined nanoscale precipitate morphology.
The approach has been verified throughout the stated Al-below-25-at.% and Mn-above-15-at.% composition window.
Extension beyond the stated composition and processing boundaries requires validation because of limitations in thermodynamic databases.
The long-term stability of the proposed nanoscale precipitate morphology remains uncertain.
TEM, synchrotron XRD, and elevated-temperature compression testing can be used to assess microstructure, phase constitution, and yield strength in these alloys.
